stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( \int_{0}^{1} f(x)\,dx = 4 \) and \( \int_{3}^{1} f(x)\,dx = 9 \). Find the value of \( \int_{3}^{0} \left(3f(x) + 2\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Join the adjacent intervals: \( \int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{1} f(x)\,dx + \int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx = 4 + (-9) = -5 \), since reversing \( \int_{3}^{1} \) changes its sign.
Reverse the requested integral: \( \int_{3}^{0} \left(3f(x) + 2\right) dx = -(3) \int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx + (2)(0 - 3) \), and the constant contributes \( -6 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, both a supplied integral and the requested one run right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.A: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.B: given integral from 3 to 1 used as if it ran from 1 to 3
distractor_derivations.C: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
